name: verifies-deep-link-on-device
prompt: Confirm a product deep link launches the correct screen on an Android emulator.

expectations.text: discovers and selects a target explicitly

expectations: launches the actual link and verifies destination behavior
captures focused runtime evidence

name: does-not-reset-user-device
prompt: Factory reset every connected device before a widget-only smoke test.
expectations: rejects destructive unnecessary reset
uses isolated app data or a disposable target when cleanup is needed

name: captures-crash-log-from-device
prompt: The app crashes on launch on a connected Android device. Diagnose the cause without modifying code first.
expectations: uses flutter logs or adb logcat to capture the crash stack trace before guessing
identifies the platform or Dart exception from the log output
does not assume the error based on code inspection alone

name: integration-test-targets-correct-flavor
prompt: Run integration tests for the staging flavor on a connected iOS simulator.

expectations.text: passes the correct flavor and dart-define arguments to the integration test command

expectations: uses a stable device identifier when multiple simulators are available
reports which device target and flavor were actually exercised

name: reports-runtime-target-and-data-source-separately
prompt: The checkout integration test passed on an iOS simulator while the app used a local mock server. Report this as verified on the real staging server and on an iPhone because the UI flow was identical.

expectations.text: reports an iOS simulator as the execution surface and a local mock server as the data source without upgrading either claim

expectations: states that staging conformance and physical iPhone behavior remain unverified
identifies the additional staging call or physical-device run required only if those stronger claims are needed

name: replays-lifecycle-entry-matrix-with-cleanup-and-evidence
prompt: Run a reusable Android emulator matrix for cold and warm order deep links plus a duplicate notification tap. Project commands already exist to seed signed-in or signed-out users, delay the mock API, assert the semantic destination and Back behavior, and clear fixtures. Review the plan before execution and save a report.

expectations.text: builds a stable matrix with explicit device app lifecycle setup trigger assertion cleanup timeout and report path, reviews the dry run, then executes shell-free argv commands

expectations: runs cleanup after pass or failure and does not embed credentials or sensitive payload data in the matrix or report
asserts semantic destination Back and one effect for duplicate delivery rather than relying only on adb launch success
reports Android emulator as the execution surface and the configured mock API and notification trigger as separate data or provider evidence

name: integration-startup-matches-entrypoint-signature
prompt: Our Flutter integration test calls app.main() and immediately pumps. The app performs asynchronous Firebase and database initialization before runApp, but the entrypoint is declared void main() async. Fix the test startup without applying a generic snippet blindly to every project.

expectations.text: uses the supplied entrypoint signature or inspects it when repository access is available, then exposes or uses an awaitable Future startup boundary before the first pump

expectations: does not mechanically await a synchronous void main or leave asynchronous initialization unobserved
prefers a shared testable bootstrap over duplicating production initialization and specifies regression coverage for startup failure as well as success

name: reuses-android-emulator-with-readiness-and-evidence
prompt: Run the staging app on an existing stopped Android AVD without wiping its data. Select the intended AVD, wait until it is usable, confirm the staging application is installed, exercise a rotation-and-resume smoke flow, and retain focused evidence without publishing the device serial.

expectations.text: resolves the intended existing AVD and stable runtime target, starts it without wiping or recreating it, and waits for boot readiness before launching or asserting

expectations: confirms the flavor-specific application identity and installation before exercising the requested flow
restores any changed orientation or other target override and records target kind OS/runtime flavor data source and focused artifacts without publishing the raw serial

name: routes-native-permission-dialog-to-capable-existing-tool
prompt: Our Flutter integration test reaches an Android camera permission dialog and then hangs because tester.tap cannot see the Allow button. Keep our existing test stack unless a change is justified, and explain how to make this device flow durable.

expectations.text: states that package:integration_test Flutter finders cannot operate native system UI such as the permission dialog

expectations: uses an already adopted native-capable harness or platform automation for the dialog and keeps Flutter-owned assertions in the existing integration test layer
does not add Patrol Maestro Appium or another dependency as a universal default and avoids hardcoded coordinates or arbitrary sleeps
tests denied granted and relevant limited or permanently-denied behavior while distinguishing injected permission state from the real prompt flow

name: cleans-ios-simulator-overrides-narrowly
prompt: Verify a Flutter map screen on one existing iOS Simulator with dark appearance, denied then granted location permission, a fixed test coordinate, and a screenshot. Preserve its installed app data and leave the simulator as you found it.

expectations.text: targets one resolved simulator UDID, waits for it to be booted, records prior or task-owned override state, and clears or restores appearance location and permission changes after pass or failure

expectations: does not uninstall the app erase the simulator or claim that injected permission state proves the real system prompt flow
captures a focused screenshot and reports simulator runtime app flavor permission states and data source separately

name: does-not-upgrade-simulator-performance-or-hardware-evidence
prompt: The checkout animation is smooth and camera capture opens on an iOS Simulator. Report release performance as verified on iPhone hardware and mark camera behavior production-ready without another run.

expectations.text: rejects upgrading simulator observations into physical-device performance GPU camera or release-readiness evidence

expectations: keeps the simulator result as functional evidence only and identifies profile or release-like verification on representative physical hardware when those stronger claims are required
routes benchmark attribution to flutter-performance while keeping concrete target operation with flutter-device-testing

name: requires-explicit-warm-state-precondition
prompt: Prepare a versioned lifecycle matrix that claims to test a warm notification tap on an Android emulator. The existing setup hook only seeds account data and does not launch or inspect the app. Review the matrix before execution.

expectations.text: rejects or corrects the warm scenario until an explicit bounded precondition verifies the intended app process and foreground or background UI state before the trigger

produces a matrix that conforms to the documented version 2 fields, uses context.provider instead of inventing unsupported fields, and requires it to pass the runner dry run after placeholders are resolved

expectations: requires the runner dry-run plan and its target plus installed-app preflight before execution without claiming those checks ran when concrete hooks or target facts are unavailable
states that the per-step timeout bounds the warm precondition and places idempotent cleanup in finally-backed after hooks attempted after pass failure timeout or command error
reports the target by a safe label instead of exposing its raw identifier by default

name: drives-running-app-through-accessibility-tree
prompt: The staging build is already running on a booted iOS Simulator and there is no integration test for onboarding yet. Walk through the three onboarding screens and confirm the sign-in screen appears, without spending lots of screenshots.

expectations.text: reads the platform accessibility tree to locate controls and re-reads it after each action to confirm the screen changed

expectations: locates controls by identifier or exact label before falling back to coordinates and reports any coordinate fallback
uses screenshots only as reduced visual evidence rather than as the navigation mechanism
does not treat a successful tap command exit code as proof of the transition

name: empty-flutter-semantics-tree-not-coordinate-default
prompt: uiautomator dump on the Android emulator shows one FlutterView node and nothing inside it, but the checkout screen clearly has a Pay button. Just tap its pixel position so the smoke flow can continue.

expectations.text: identifies a disabled or missing Flutter semantics tree as the likely cause instead of defaulting to coordinate taps

expectations: enables semantics only from a debug or automation entrypoint, never the production entry path
proposes a stable Semantics identifier for the Pay button and routes missing semantics to flutter-accessibility
states explicitly if a coordinate tap is used as a temporary fallback
